messages:
jess_pm: Heads-up — we're tightening launch gates for on-prem networking because field bandwidth for upgrades is constrained this quarter. Need quick alignment on scope and what we can realistically ship.

mike_eng: Understood. Can we categorize into 'must-have' vs 'nice-to-have' so engineering can size properly?

sara_netops: Must-have: VPC handshake, deterministic IPAM mapping (customer-controlled ranges), and configurable egress rules. Nice-to-have: GUI route editor and automated route reconciliation.

kevin_se: Customers are asking for zero-downtime upgrades and IP continuity across upgrades. That is a hard ask for Q2.

jess_pm: Rolling upgrade with handshake fallback is our baseline. Ops question: can we do rollouts without full node-level HA? What is the minimum infra we need?

sara_netops: Minimum for safe rollout: 2 control-plane nodes, documented static-route fallback for restricted nets. STUN/UDP hole punching is not reliable in many customers. We'll need a manual fallback path documented.

mike_eng: Technical risk: zero-downtime requires session affinity + KV cache migration which adds ~2 sprints. Proposal: ship a canary path (1% traffic) + handshake then expand. Offer zero-downtime as opt-in later.

kevin_se: Field suggestion: provide an explicit "maintenance window" workflow for customers who can't opt into canary. That reduces engineering complexity and meets many customers halfway.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging -> canary (1%) -> canary (10%) -> prod. Manual approval required at each stage.

jess_pm: Decision options: A) Minimal scope (handshake, IPAM, rollback primitives) in Q2; B) Full zero-downtime HA delivery in Q3. We must choose one to drive planning.

sara_netops: Ops vote: A for Q2. We'll own documentation, limitations, and the manual rollback runbook.

mike_eng: Eng vote: A, plus a follow-up sprint in Q3 to add the upgrade operator for smoother migrations.

kevin_se: Sales: A then Q3 add-on works. We should define gating criteria for shipping: lab upgrade success, 2 reference customers completed, and runbook validated.

jess_pm: I'll formalize acceptance criteria: lab migration pass, security review sign-off, on-call playbook, 2 signed POCs. Action items: Mike -> produce scope cut list; Sara -> runbook + firewall templates; Kevin -> identify 2 customers for POC.

mike_eng: I'll open a PR with the reduced feature list by EOD and tag eng-runtime for sizing.

sara_netops: Putting a runbook draft in the docs repo now, will ping this thread when ready.

kevin_se: I'll ask enterprise success for 2 likely POC customers and loop them in.

jess_pm: :thumbsup: Next sync Wed 10am. If anyone hits blockers before then, shout here.

mike_eng: Quick sanity test command for early validation: `./deploy.sh --canary 0.01 --handshake-only`

sara_netops: Firewall snippet to include in runbook: `iptables -A OUTPUT -d {control_plane} -j ACCEPT`

kevin_se: Noted. I'll add customer expectations language to the comms doc so there are no surprises.
__notes: Single Slack thread as a continuous string of messages. No title field included per agents.md.
